neighbours.label: Comma closing a factual clause in explanatory prose just before a concession ('stays fairly constant, although ...')
fire: The number of nerve cells in the adult brain stays roughly the same, although new connections form all the time.
Most of the heat escapes through the roof of the house, although the walls also lose some.
The salt content of the ocean remains fairly stable, although it varies near river mouths.
The total amount of water on Earth is nearly constant, although its form keeps changing.
Your resting heart rate stays fairly steady through the day, although stress can raise it.
The size of the colony stays about the same each year, although individual bees are replaced.
The basic recipe has barely changed in a century, although the ingredients have improved.
The amount of bone in the skeleton stays fairly constant, although old tissue is constantly replaced.
quiet: The number of nerve cells in the adult brain is about eighty six billion.
Most of the heat escapes through the roof of the house in winter.
The salt content of the ocean is about thirty five grams per liter.
The total amount of water on Earth is about one billion cubic kilometers.
Your resting heart rate is measured best in the early morning.
The size of the colony is measured by counting bees at the entrance.
The basic recipe calls for flour, butter, sugar and two eggs.
The amount of bone in the skeleton is measured with a special scan.
